Synopsis:
    A blowout August jobs report (+162K NFP, ~3x expectations, labor force participation at 61.6%) has reignited debate over a Fed rate hike at the September 15–16 FOMC meeting. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh struck a hawkish tone at Jackson Hole, and market odds of a September hike have risen to ~62%. The decision now hinges on next Friday's CPI and PPI prints. Political noise is elevated — President Trump is threatening trade embargoes with deficit countries unless the Fed cuts rates, though Warsh has so far avoided direct personal criticism. Wage growth at 3.1% remains contained, keeping some officials comfortable on hold. Nationwide's chief economist now forecasts two 25bp hikes by year-end, lifting the fed funds rate to 4.00–4.25%.
